originality.rationale: The motivating 2026 full text derives the FST quadrature and reports a numerical return to pairwise-like behavior but does not state the sharp positive s^(d-1) deviation or the opposite t^(d-1)/d fixed-target law. The 2023 pairwise FST paper concerns distributional pairwise synchronization, not a variable interaction order. Semantic searches of published research results had no direct duplicate; closest synchronization results concern distinct finite triads or control optimization. The general integral representation supplies the starting formula but does not establish its nonuniform moving-target asymptotics without a separate argument.
residual_risks: The foundational 2023 first-synchronization-time article was available in abstract rather than full text, although its pairwise model is structurally distinct.
No search establishes global historical uniqueness; generic moving-threshold perturbation techniques or unindexed later papers could subsume an equivalent formulation.
Claims concern the reduced continuum model only; no finite-network transfer is verified.

value.rationale: First synchronization time is a concrete experimentally motivated transient observable. The known high-order coupling-speed paradox is resolved by identifying an endogenous moving-target displacement that dominates the strictly positive pointwise speedup. The exact coefficient and two different exponential bases explain both sign and convergence speed uniformly over a meaningful multi-parameter monostable regime, with a natural fixed-threshold control experiment. It is not a single artificial parameter computation or an incremental finite enumeration.
